description: Physics-lumped SMES: magnetic energy E=0.5*L*I^2 stored in a superconducting coil, charged/discharged through a power-conditioning chopper that imposes the coil terminal voltage V_L = L*dI/dt. Coil-current ODE integrated with scipy.solve_ivp. Near-lossless coil (tiny equivalent series resistance in superconducting state) plus converter conduction/switching losses and continuous cryogenic refrigeration parasitic load.

unit.name: Generic HTS SMES Unit, 10 MJ / 2 MW
unit.source: Hassenzahl, W.V. (2001) 'Superconducting magnetic energy storage', IEEE Trans. Appl. Supercond. 11(1):1447-1453. Buckles & Hassenzahl (2000) IEEE Power Eng. Rev. 20(5):16-20. Ali, M.H., Wu, B. & Dougal, R.A. (2010) 'An overview of SMES applications in power and energy systems', IEEE Trans. Sustain. Energy 1(1):38-47.

I_max_A.note: Maximum coil current at E_max = 10 MJ (critical-current limited)

V_dc_max_V.note: Max DC-link / chopper terminal voltage magnitude applied to coil

R_coil_ohm.note: Equivalent series resistance of coil+leads in superconducting state (joint+lead residual; ~0.1 microohm)

eta_converter.note: Power-conditioning chopper efficiency per pass (VSC/IGBT chopper)

P_conv_loss_frac.note: Reserved; converter loss derived from eta_converter

T_op_K.note: Coil operating temperature (HTS REBCO/MgB2 with GM cooler)

P_cryo_MW.note: Continuous cryogenic refrigeration electrical input (heat leak removal via GM/pulse-tube cooler, ~30 kW for 10 MJ HTS, Hassenzahl 2001)

P_request_MW.note: Positive = discharge to grid, negative = charge from grid
